blocks.text: Elastography measures how stiff the liver is. Scar is one cause; inflammation, cholestasis, congestion and food are others. No pediatric cut-off is endorsed by AASLD (2025) or WFUMB (2024). Read every value with the child's ALT, bilirubin, heart and last meal, and against the child's own earlier values.

Short breath-hold; few child norms per vendor
Works in infants, in free breathing

blocks.h: A valid reading in a child

sub: Method, probe and vendor: each platform has its own normal.
Fast if possible; an infant: scan just before the next feed (expert opinion: stiffness rises after a meal).
No sedation if avoidable: sedation raises stiffness (Li 2020).
At least 10 valid shots and IQR/median ≤ 30% (Lewindon 2019; WFUMB 2024).
Invalid readings cluster in young children: reliable without sedation from about 6 years (Engelmann 2012).
Probe by chest circumference: S1 < 45 cm, S2 45–75 cm, M > 75 cm (Engelmann 2012).
Same machine, same probe, same conditions every time.

blocks.text: Table: 240 healthy children, Heidelberg (Engelmann 2012). Pooled data from 652 healthy children gave 2.45–5.56 kPa (Li 2020); age, sedation, S-probe use and steatosis pushed values up. On different machines in the same 4–17-year-olds, median 3.3 kPa on 2D-SWE vs 4.1 kPa on pSWE and VCTE (Mjelle 2019).

sub: Acute viral hepatitis pushed stiffness into the cirrhosis range at the ALT peak (Arena 2008, adults).
Children and young adults with F0–F2: higher ALT, more often > 8.6 kPa; no effect once F3–F4 (Raizner 2017, 154 patients).
Stiffness fell after biliary drainage, irrespective of fibrosis (Millonig 2008, adults).
Stiffness tracks central venous pressure (Millonig 2010, adults).
Fontan children: median 18.6 vs 4.7 kPa in controls (Chen 2016). Follow the child's own trend.
Food, infiltration (HLH, storage disease, leukemia), and moderate-to-severe steatosis (AASLD 2025).
Measure after drainage, decongestion, or once the ALT has settled. Otherwise do not stage.

blocks.text: Baveno VII "rule of five" (< 10 kPa rules out, > 15 kPa rules in compensated advanced chronic liver disease; < 20 kPa with platelets ≥ 150 × 10⁹/L skips screening endoscopy) is adult. WFUMB 2024: no pediatric cut-off can be recommended. Do not skip an endoscopy in a child on the adult rule.

sub: Stiffness pooled: sensitivity 83%, specificity 79% for atresia (Wagner 2022, 11 studies).
2D-SWE > 1.84 m/s: sensitivity 92%, specificity 79% (Dillman 2019, 41 infants).
A high value raises urgency. A low value never delays biopsy or cholangiogram.
Cirrhosis (F4): sensitivity 96%, specificity 89%; varices: 85% / 76% (Wagner 2022).
Spleen stiffness ≥ 28.9 kPa: AUROC 0.87 vs 0.73 for liver stiffness; sensitivity 75%, specificity 87% (Sintusek 2019, 51 children).
No variceal bleed with spleen stiffness < 60 kPa (Goldschmidt 2014, 99 children, 19 scoped). Small series: never use it to skip endoscopy.
5.55 kPa flags CF liver disease: sensitivity 70%, specificity 82% (Lewindon 2019, 160 children).
8.7 kPa separates F3–F4 from F1–F2: sensitivity 75%, specificity 100%; with APRI, AUROC 0.92 (Lewindon 2019).
Advanced fibrosis: AUROC 0.67, PPV 40%, NPV 90% (Nichols 2026, NASH CRN, 92 children). A rule-out test at best.
ESPGHAN 2026: < 5.5 kPa may help exclude significant fibrosis; > 10 kPa suggests advanced chronic liver disease (MASLD only, low evidence). AASLD 2025: adult thresholds not validated in children.
Congestion dominates: trend only, never stage from one value.

blocks.text: CAP (fat on VCTE) did not separate steatosis grades in pediatric MASLD: medians 325, 310 and 323 dB/m for grades 1–3 (Nichols 2026). AASLD 2025 advises against diagnostic CAP in children; ESPGHAN 2026 accepts it as an adjunct. MRE samples the whole liver and is least affected by obesity and ascites, but its kPa is shear stiffness: never compare it with ultrasound kPa. Use MRE when an MRI is needed anyway or ultrasound fails.

sub: Built in adults with hepatitis C (Wai 2003). Muscle, hemolysis and a hepatitis flare raise AST; hypersplenism lowers platelets.
Depends on the lab's AST ULN.
Built in adults with hepatitis B (Lemoine 2016). Meaningless in early infancy, when GGT is physiologically high.
Contains age in years: low in children. Never reassure with a low FIB-4.
Cystic fibrosis: APRI > 0.264 (Leung 2015) and GPR > 0.20 (Calvopina 2022) flag liver disease. CFF 2024: calculate at least one index and follow it at least yearly.
Adolescent hepatitis B without elastography: APRI > 0.5 significant fibrosis, > 1.0 cirrhosis (WHO 2024).
MASLD: APRI AUROC 0.76, FIB-4 0.61 for F ≥ 3; none beat ALT > 50 U/L (Kalveram 2024, 457 children). AASLD 2025 and ESPGHAN 2026: do not use.

items.text: Pooled upper limit of normal VCTE: 5.56 kPa (Li 2020); age-specific upper limits reach 6.8 kPa in teens (Engelmann 2012). Age, sedation, S-probe and fat push values up.
Each platform has its own normal: 2D-SWE reads lower than pSWE and VCTE in the same child (Mjelle 2019).
Inflammation, cholestasis and congestion each make a non-cirrhotic liver read like cirrhosis. Stage after the cause settles.
In biliary atresia, stiffness ranks the infant; the cholangiogram decides.
After the Kasai, spleen stiffness ≥ 28.9 kPa: AUROC 0.87 vs 0.73 for liver stiffness; sensitivity 75%, specificity 87% (Sintusek 2019).
Pediatric MASLD: VCTE is a rule-out test (NPV 90%, PPV 40%); CAP cannot grade fat (Nichols 2026).
MRE kPa and ultrasound kPa live on different scales. Never compare them.
FIB-4 < 1.30 does not reassure in a child: the age term makes it low.

positions.wfumb_2024_elastography: None can be recommended; ≤ 5 kPa rules out, ≥ 15 kPa rules in, except biliary atresia, CF and Fontan

rows.note: Use the WFUMB rule-out value (≤ 5 kPa) only outside biliary atresia, CF and congestion.

positions.espghan_2026_masld: May help: < 5.5 kPa to exclude significant fibrosis, > 10 kPa suggests advanced chronic liver disease

rows.note: Between 5.5 and 10 kPa ESPGHAN gives no answer and AASLD gives no threshold: decide on the whole picture, not the number.

positions.espghan_2026_masld: May be an adjunct; > 280 dB/m strongly associated with steatosis

rows.note: CAP did not track histologic grade (Nichols 2026).

positions.aasld_2025_masld_peds: Adult cut-offs should not be applied
positions.espghan_2026_masld: FIB-4, APRI, PNFI, PNFS not recommended

rows.note: Do not reassure with a low FIB-4 or APRI.

rows.topic: Serum scores, pediatric chronic liver disease (not MASLD)

positions.aasld_2025_blood_nilda: Suggests APRI or FIB-4 for F3–F4 (ungraded, low evidence); not for monitoring
positions.cff_2024_cfld: Cystic fibrosis: at least one index (APRI, GPR or FIB-4), at least yearly
positions.espghan_2026_masld: MASLD: FIB-4, APRI, PNFI, PNFS not recommended

rows.note: Scores help most in cystic fibrosis and as a trend in one child; never as a single staging value.

positions.aasld_2025_imaging_nilda: Not a standalone test of regression or progression
positions.wfumb_2024_elastography: Same machine and probe; a change > 10% is meaningful

rows.note: Confirm any change with the clinical picture.

positions.baveno_vi_peds_2016: Children: no noninvasive rule to skip endoscopy
